findings.description: Success criterion 2 ("A fixture programme can create one phase, one loop, and one external task on every target host") is not met as written. loop-007-7's own measurement, run this attempt, states plainly: "Criterion 2 is met on codex, cursor and opencode, and failed on claude-code." The claude-code adapter ships no shared router skill and no envelope writer, and its own installed .claude/commands/next-loop.md:355-359 states that migrating it to emit an envelope is a Phase 7 item. Unlike criterion 1, which was formally rewritten in plan.md on 2026-09-03 with a dated note explaining why its subject changed, criterion 2's text in plan.md was never amended, narrowed, or given an operator-recorded waiver for the claude-code gap. The programme's own stated rule in loop-007's 'Hard rules' (do not narrow a criterion to fit the result without recording the reason) was followed for criterion 1 and not for criterion 2 -- the evidence quietly declares partial success against an unconditional criterion instead.
findings.evidence: .advanced-plans/phases/phase-6/plan.md line 59 (unconditional 'on every target host', no rewrite note, contrast with criterion 1's note at lines 66-99); .advanced-plans/evidence/2026-09-03-loop-007-7-fixture-programme-four-hosts.md 'Criterion 2, scored' section (met on codex/cursor/opencode, failed on claude-code); .advanced-plans/phases/phase-6/loops.md line 1142 (loop-007-7 result text, same conclusion).

findings.location: advanced-planning: .advanced-plans/phases/phase-6/loops.md (loop-007-8 and loop-007-9 result text, loop-007-10 result text); commits 05d1e55, 0f138de
findings.description: The loop record makes a specific, checkable claim about commit content that is false when the cited commit is actually opened -- the same defect class the programme names ('a citation nobody opened is a claim, not a reference'), found here in its own evidence trail. loop-007-8's and loop-007-9's result text both state that commits 05d1e55 and 0f138de 'carry no opencode attribution trailer.' Both commits, read directly, contain a 'Co-Authored-By: opencode (Qwen) via herdr worker <name>' trailer verbatim in the original commit message, not added by later amendment: git reflog shows a single 'commit:' entry at each hash, not 'commit (amend)'. loop-007-10's result compounds the error, calling a later commit (3949abd) 'the first worker commit in this programme to carry its attribution trailers,' which is false since two earlier commits in the same history already carried one.
findings.evidence: git log -1 --format=%B on 05d1e55 and 0f138de in the loop-008-gate worktree shows the trailers present at commit creation; git reflog show loop-008-gate shows no rebase/amend at those entries. Compare loops.md loop-007-8 result ('Worker commit carries no opencode attribution trailer'), loop-007-9 result (same claim for 0f138de), and loop-007-10 result ('3949abd is the first worker commit in this programme to carry its attribution trailers').

findings.description: The module docstring still states, of the loop-complete path, that path scope is not validated and that there is no commit-stage path-scope enforcement today. This was true before the F1 fix (loop-008-8) and is false after it: the loop-complete subcommand now derives the changed set from git and runs validate_path_scope over it. Self-disclosed in loops.md as 'not fixed here, deliberately,' but it remains live in the shipped module and would mislead a reader deciding whether commit-stage enforcement exists.
findings.evidence: .advanced-plans/evidence/2026-09-03-loop-008-8-gate-defects-closed.md, 'A stale docstring the fix left behind' section, quoting the exact docstring text and naming it false after F1.

findings.description: The three gate failure modes (path-scope violation, VACUOUS, schema failure) deliberately share exit code 1 and are distinguished only by stderr prefix (path_scope:, vacuous:, schema:); an explicit, recorded design decision in loop-008-9 rather than an oversight, now recorded in main()'s docstring. Recorded for completeness per loop-008's own success-criteria audit; not a defect.
findings.evidence: .advanced-plans/evidence/2026-09-03-loop-008-success-criteria-audit.md, item 1388; verified live in platforms/python/evidence_gate.py (path_scope:, vacuous:, schema:, git: prefixes at the cited lines).

findings.description: F5 (loop-008-8) made the resume/finalize branch refuse to finalize rather than run the gate on a possibly-stale baseline; a stated consequence is that this branch no longer runs state_validate on loop-ready.json at all. A deliberate, disclosed trade-off with a stated reason, not a silent regression.
findings.evidence: .advanced-plans/evidence/2026-09-03-loop-008-8-gate-defects-closed.md, 'F5: the decision, and the difficulty it names'.

failure_notes: Criterion 2 (a fixture programme can create one phase, one loop, and one external task on every target host) is unmet on claude-code and plan.md was never amended to narrow or waive it, unlike criterion 1's dated rewrite. Before the next gate attempt, either (a) give the claude-code adapter a shared router / envelope writer so it completes the fixture programme like the other three hosts, or (b) have the operator explicitly amend plan.md's criterion 2 the same way criterion 1 was amended -- recording that claude-code's envelope gap is a named, disclosed limitation carried to Phase 7 -- so the criterion is judged against text that matches what the phase can actually ship. Loops involved: loop-007-7 (measurement), and whichever future loop performs the fix or the amendment.

Correct the false attribution claims in loops.md for loop-007-8, loop-007-9 and loop-007-10: commits 05d1e55 and 0f138de already carry their opencode worker trailers, contrary to what those loops' result text says. This does not change any code but the loop record is evidence other reviewers and the operator rely on, and it is currently wrong on a directly checkable fact.

The stale evidence_gate.py module docstring (describing loop-complete as not path-scope-validated, which F1 made false) should be corrected by whichever loop next touches that module, as loop-008-8 itself recommended.

Full suite independently re-run by this reviewer in the subject worktree: 1099 passed, 1 skipped, matching loop-007-10's reported count exactly.
